summary: Layer 1B expanded the dispatchable-generation power-island node with a two-lane universe: GE Vernova as the obvious reference anchor for gas turbine slot scarcity and service backlog, plus underfollowed second-order names where the exposure hides in emissions/exhaust systems or distribution/service businesses rather than obvious AI, utility, or power-equipment labels. The most relevant underfollowed candidates from this pass are CECO Environmental, tied to engineered emissions/exhaust systems and natural-gas power-generation backlog, and Kirby, whose Distribution and Services segment has become a power-generation equipment, parts, and service beneficiary with explicit references to behind-the-meter and backup power demand.
